blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Ezekiel 38-39 depicts Gog of the land of Magog leading a latter-day coalition against restored Israel and being defeated by divine action. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. Interpretations differ on some details.

A literary feature to notice is that Papyrus 967 places the material conventionally numbered Ezekiel 38-39 before chapter 37, showing an ancient order different from the familiar Masoretic sequence. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.
